name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Pain Management Neural Implant
product_name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Pain Management Neural Implant
description: A neural interface application that gives the user conscious control over their pain perception — the ability to dial pain sensation from full intensity to zero on a mental slider. The PMNI intercepts pain signals at the spinal cord level and modulates their transmission to the brain based on user-set thresholds. At zero setting, the user feels no pain whatsoever. At intermediate settings, pain is attenuated to informational — you know you have been injured, but it does not hurt. The system includes an override that forces pain back to full intensity if life-threatening injury is detected, preventing users from ignoring fatal damage.
enables: Selective pain awareness for injury monitoring
social_impact: PMNI has created a population segment that literally does not feel pain — and the behavioral consequences are significant. PMNI users take physical risks that pain-feeling individuals avoid, sustain injuries they do not notice, and develop a relationship with their bodies that is fundamentally different from the human norm. The technology has also created new forms of exploitation — workers with PMNI can be pushed past safe physical limits because they do not experience the warning signals of injury.
story_hooks: A PMNI user's life-threat override failed to activate during a critical injury — they bled out without feeling any pain, unaware they were dying until they lost consciousness.
Employers in Tier 2 industrial zones are requiring PMNI installation as a condition of employment — workers who cannot feel pain are more productive, and the injury rates are being hidden.
